resources.string: Your passwords, only on this device
Set up a screen lock (PIN, pattern or biometrics) on your device to use Password Memory.
Use your biometrics or device PIN
Authenticate again to unlock the encryption key
Add your first entry and it will stay on this device only.
Stored encrypted: you can view and copy it whenever you want.
Careful: a hashed password cannot be recovered. You will only be able to check guesses against it.
Free text to help you remember it.
Leave it empty to keep the current password.
This password is hashed and cannot be changed. Delete the entry and create a new one.
Password copied. The clipboard clears in %1$s.
This password could not be decrypted. The key may have been lost after a reinstall: restore a backup to recover it.
This password is not stored: type it to check whether it is the right one. There is no limit on attempts.
That is it. You can copy it now.

The encryption key never leaves this device, so a backup file is the only way to move your entries to another device or recover them after a reinstall. The file is encrypted with a one-time passphrase that is not saved anywhere: if you forget it, the backup is unusable.
Save an encrypted file with all your entries.
Restore entries from a backup file.
Choose a passphrase to encrypt the backup file. You will need it to import it later.
Enter the passphrase used when the backup was exported.
Wrong passphrase, or the file is not a valid backup.
The operation could not be completed.
Password Memory is your autofill service
Android will ask this app to fill your logins, and to save the passwords you type.
Another service, usually Google, is filling and saving your passwords.
This device does not offer an autofill service.

Once it is on: tap a username or password field and your entries show up over the keyboard. When you type a new password anywhere, the \"Save password\" prompt is this app\'s, and the entry lands here encrypted.
Password Memory builds suggestions locally and does not send them over the network. A password is released to the destination app only after you unlock; that app controls how it is used afterward.
There are no entries that can be filled. Hashed passwords cannot be recovered, so they are not offered here.
The password could not be saved.
Bring in passwords exported as a CSV file.

Export your passwords first:

• On this phone: Settings › Google › Autofill › Google Password Manager › Settings › Export passwords.
• On a computer: Chrome › chrome://password-manager/settings › Export.

Then pick the file here. Everything is imported as encrypted entries.
That file holds every password in plain text. Delete it as soon as the import is done.

That file is not a password export. Look for the CSV you exported from Google or Chrome.
Your passwords are safely stored now. The CSV still holds them in plain text, so deleting it is the safe thing to do.
Remember to delete the CSV: it holds your passwords in plain text.
How long Password Memory may stay open after you switch to another app.
A copied password is wiped from the clipboard after this long.
Screenshots and screen recording are blocked throughout the app, and the recents preview stays blank. That cannot be turned off.
The wipe happens while the app is still running. If Android closes it first, the copy is left behind — it is flagged as sensitive, so it never shows in the clipboard preview.
